display.$description: Display stack used for portfolio headings and titles.

body.$description: Body stack used for interface and editorial copy.

mono.$description: Monospace stack used for metadata and technical labels.

light.$description: Light weight used for large editorial typography.

regular.$description: Regular weight used for default body copy.

medium.$description: Medium weight used for compact emphasis.

semibold.$description: Semibold weight used for prominent card titles.

label.$description: Compact 12-pixel size used by uppercase, letter-spaced labels and eyebrows (metadata card labels, section eyebrows, chips).

caption.$description: Caption size used for supporting metadata.

bodySmall.$description: Small body size used for secondary interface copy.

body.$description: Default body size used for readable interface copy.

bodyLarge.$description: Large body size used for lead and editorial copy.

title.$description: Title size used for module and section titles.

heading.$description: Heading size used for major case-study sections.

display.$description: Display size used for the largest case-study headings.

heroMin.$description: Lower bound of the fluid hero heading size.

heroMax.$description: Upper bound of the fluid hero heading size.

tight.$description: Letter spacing in em for display type: titles, headings, the hero.

normal.$description: Letter spacing in em for running text.

eyebrow.$description: Letter spacing in em for uppercase labels, eyebrows, and chips.

none.$description: Line height for single-line chips and dots.

hero.$description: Line height for the fluid hero heading.

tight.$description: Line height for tight multi-line titles.

title.$description: Line height for module and section titles.

snug.$description: Line height for compact supporting copy.

label.$description: Line height for labels and captions.

body.$description: Line height for interface copy at the default size.

none.$description: Square corner treatment for elements without rounding.

small.$description: Subtle corner treatment for compact controls.

base.$description: Default corner treatment matching the current rounded-lg utility.

large.$description: Large corner treatment used by portfolio media and modules.

round.$description: Fully rounded treatment used for circular and pill elements.

fast.$description: Fast duration used for immediate interaction feedback.

medium.$description: Medium duration used for standard interface transitions.

slow.$description: Slow duration used for deliberate reveal transitions.

page.$description: Page duration used by route and header movement.

reveal.$description: Reveal duration used when content enters the viewport: card entrances, scroll reveals, and editorial staggers.

ambient.$description: Ambient duration used for repeating decorative motion.

enter.$description: Expressive deceleration used when content enters.

move.$description: Smooth movement curve used for spatial transitions.

standard.$description: Standard material curve used for balanced state changes.

settle.$description: Plain deceleration (CSS ease-out) used by fades and small hover moves.

exit.$description: Acceleration (CSS ease-in) used when something leaves.

ambient.$description: Symmetric curve used by calm repeating motion.

compact.$description: Space between page sections on narrow screens.

wide.$description: Space between page sections from the md breakpoint.

compact.$description: Space between modules inside a case-study section on narrow screens.

compact.$description: Gap between the blocks of a module stack on narrow screens.

wide.$description: Gap between the blocks of a module stack from md.

compact.$description: Space between a figure or title and the line beneath it on narrow screens.

wide.$description: Space between a figure or title and the line beneath it from md.

guide.$description: The sticky case-study section guide; above the header so its taps win while the header re-reveals.

overlay.$description: Full-screen overlays: About, the preview bar, the publish dialog.

modal.$description: Topmost modal surfaces: the image and video lightboxes and the publish dialog.
